summary_en: Tokugawa Ieyasu's great castle, where the rebuilt Hommaru Palace glows with gold-leaf paintings. The main keep is closed for now.
description_en: Tokugawa Ieyasu ordered the castle built in 1610, and it was home to the Owari Tokugawa for more than two centuries. Air raids in May 1945 destroyed most of it; the keep, crowned with golden shachihoko, was rebuilt in concrete in 1959.
The Hommaru Palace was rebuilt with traditional joinery and opened in full in 2018. Its sliding doors are painted with tigers, pheasants and cherry blossoms in the Kano-school style.

Come in late March or early April, when about 900 cherry trees bloom across the grounds. The free English volunteer tours are not held from 29 December to 4 January, and were paused from 22 June to 30 September in 2026.
highlights_en: Golden shachihoko on the keep roof
Free English tours at 12:30 most days
opening_hours: 9:00–16:30. Last entry to the Hommaru Palace and the Nishinomaru Treasure House is 16:00, and both are about a 10-minute walk from the gates. Hours are longer on some festival evenings, such as cherry-blossom season.
nearest_station: Nagoyajo Station (Meijo subway line, M07), Exit 7
access_en: Nagoyajo Station (Meijo Line, M07), Exit 7, then a 5-minute walk to the East Gate. From Nagoya Station: Higashiyama Line to Sakae, change to the Meijo Line (Clockwise) for two stops; about 15 minutes, ¥240.

legs.note_en: Follow the yellow subway signs to the Higashiyama Line.
Change here. Follow the purple signs to the Meijo Line platform marked Clockwise (右回り) for Nagoyajo and Ozone.
Called Shiyakusho (市役所) until January 2023, so older maps and some bus stops still use that name.

legs.text_en: Take Exit 7. You come up by Nagoya City Hall, the building with a castle-style roof. Walk to the castle's East Gate.

alternatives.text_en: From stop 11 at the Nagoya Station bus terminal to the Nagoya Castle stop, a minute from the Main Gate. Runs Tuesday to Sunday (if Monday is a holiday, it runs then and rests on Tuesday). One-day pass ¥500.
Sakae 13 stops right at the Main Gate (Nagoya-jo Seimon-mae).

admission_en: Adults ¥1,000; junior high school age and under free. The castle ticket includes the Hommaru Palace. A combined ticket with the Tokugawa-en garden is ¥1,040 (cash only). Cards and e-money are accepted at the ticket counter, and tickets can also be bought online through asoview.

reasons_en: The rebuilt Hommaru Palace is the real draw: room after room of gold-leaf sliding-door paintings, finished with traditional joinery. Few places in Japan let you walk through a palace like this.
Easy for first-timers. It is a short subway ride from Nagoya Station, and free English volunteer tours leave the Main and East gates at 12:30 most days.
Why not five: the main keep has been closed for years, so you can admire it and its golden shachihoko only from outside, and the palace can have a long queue.

route_en.title_en: Start early and go straight to the Hommaru Palace
route_en.text_en: Enter at 9:00 and head for the palace first, about 10 minutes from either gate. Queues build from late morning; the posted wait can reach 40 minutes.

route_en.title_en: Look up at the keep and its golden shachihoko
route_en.text_en: The keep is closed, but the Honmaru courtyard right beside the palace gives the classic close-up of its green roofs and the two golden shachihoko.

route_en.title_en: Walk the stone walls to the Southwest Corner Watchtower
route_en.text_en: Follow the moat to one of the few Edo-period buildings that survived 1945. It is usually seen from outside; the inside opens only during some festivals.
On the east side of the grounds, this designated scenic garden is a calm stop before you leave by the East Gate.

Just outside the gates. The Yoshinao zone by the Main Gate serves Nagoya classics such as miso-nikomi udon, hitsumabushi and miso katsu; the Muneharu zone by the East Gate is more modern and stays open into the evening.
